ferriter-s-cove.name: Ferriter's Cove
ferriter-s-cove.summary: A small bay at the westernmost point of Ireland's Dingle Peninsula in County Kerry.

dingle-peninsula.name: Dingle Peninsula
dingle-peninsula.summary: The northernmost of the major peninsulas in County Kerry, Ireland, ending at Dunmore Head, the westernmost point of mainland Ireland.

c-ide-fields.name: Céide Fields
c-ide-fields.summary: An extensive prehistoric landscape on Ireland's north Mayo coast, with stone field walls, dwellings and megalithic monuments buried beneath blanket bog, traditionally dated to the Neolithic farming era.

county-mayo.name: County Mayo
county-mayo.summary: A county in the west of Ireland, in the province of Connacht, named after the village now known as Mayo Abbey; its present boundaries date to 1585.

early-european-farmers.name: Early European Farmers
early-european-farmers.summary: A population that carried farming from Anatolia into Europe and Northwest Africa from around 7,000 BC, gradually mixing with local hunter-gatherer groups.

chassey-le-camp.name: Chassey-le-Camp
chassey-le-camp.summary: A small commune in the Saône-et-Loire department of eastern France.

sa-ne-et-loire.name: Saône-et-Loire
sa-ne-et-loire.summary: A department in the Bourgogne-Franche-Comté region of France, named after the Saône and Loire rivers, with its prefecture at Mâcon.

wayland-s-smithy.name: Wayland's Smithy
wayland-s-smithy.summary: An Early Neolithic chambered long barrow near Ashbury, Oxfordshire, completed around 3430 BCE, among the finest surviving examples of its regional type of monument in Britain.

west-kennet-long-barrow.name: West Kennet Long Barrow
west-kennet-long-barrow.summary: A Neolithic chambered tomb near Avebury in Wiltshire, England, probably built in the 37th century BC and used for burials for centuries afterward.

gavrinis.name: Gavrinis
gavrinis.summary: A small island in Brittany, France, containing a Neolithic passage tomb built around 4200–4000 BCE, one of the world's oldest surviving buildings, decorated with megalithic art.

knap-of-howar.name: Knap of Howar
knap-of-howar.summary: A Neolithic farmstead on Papa Westray, Orkney, occupied from 3800 to 2800 BC, possibly the oldest preserved stone house in northern Europe.

papa-westray.name: Papa Westray
papa-westray.summary: One of Scotland's Orkney Islands, known for its fertile soil and home to the Neolithic Knap of Howar farmstead; its 2022 population was 95.

maeshowe.name: Maeshowe
maeshowe.summary: Neolithic chambered cairn and passage grave on Orkney, Scotland, built around 2800 BC and part of the "Heart of Neolithic Orkney" UNESCO World Heritage Site.

standing-stones-of-stenness.name: Stenness
standing-stones-of-stenness.summary: A Neolithic monument near Stromness on Orkney, Scotland, possibly the oldest henge site in the British Isles and part of a World Heritage Site.

orkney.name: Orkney
orkney.summary: An archipelago off northern Scotland with about 70 islands, inhabited for at least 10,000 years and once part of the Kingdom of Norway before joining Scotland in 1472.

links-of-noltland.name: Links of Noltland
links-of-noltland.summary: A large prehistoric settlement on Orkney's Westray island with late Neolithic and early Bronze Age dwellings, where the Westray Wife figurine was found in 2009.

westray-wife.name: Westray Wife
westray-wife.summary: A small Neolithic figurine carved from sandstone, discovered in Orkney, Scotland in 2009; the earliest known depiction of a human face found in the UK.

henge.name: Henge
henge.summary: A Neolithic earthwork with a circular bank and internal ditch, not built for defense; some enclosed stone or timber circles like Avebury and Stonehenge.

le-grand-pressigny.name: Le Grand-Pressigny
le-grand-pressigny.summary: A commune in central France known for a Chalcolithic flint mine that produced prized caramel-coloured stone traded across Europe.

linear-pottery-culture.name: Linear Pottery culture
linear-pottery-culture.summary: A major European Neolithic archaeological culture (about 5500–4500 BC), marking early agriculture's spread along the Danube, Elbe and Rhine, named for its simple incised pottery.

storegga-slide.name: Storegga Slide
storegga-slide.summary: One of the largest known submarine landslides, off Norway's coast around 6200 BCE, which triggered a massive tsunami across the North Atlantic.

doggerland.name: Doggerland
doggerland.summary: A now-submerged area of land in Northern Europe that once connected Britain to the mainland, flooded by rising seas between about 10,000 and 7,000 years ago.

cardium-pottery.name: Cardium pottery
cardium-pottery.summary: A Neolithic decorative pottery style made by pressing cockle shells into wet clay, giving its name to the 'Cardial culture' that produced and spread it across the western Mediterranean.

saint-michel-tumulus.name: Saint-Michel tumulus
saint-michel-tumulus.summary: Megalithic grave mound near Carnac in Brittany, France, and the largest grave mound in continental Europe.

sweet-track.name: Sweet Track
sweet-track.summary: A Neolithic timber causeway across the Somerset Levels in England, built in 3807 BC and used for only about ten years before rising water forced its abandonment.

somerset-levels.name: Somerset Levels
somerset-levels.summary: A low-lying coastal plain and wetland region of Somerset, England, home to some of the earliest evidence of human activity in Britain, including the world's oldest known timber trackway.

newgrange.name: Newgrange
newgrange.summary: A Neolithic passage tomb in County Meath, Ireland, built around 3100 BC, older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids, aligned so sunlight floods its chamber at the winter solstice.

br-na-b-inne.name: Brú na Bóinne
br-na-b-inne.summary: Ancient Neolithic monument complex in Ireland's Boyne Valley, including the passage tombs of Newgrange, Knowth and Dowth, built in the 32nd century BC.

knowth.name: Knowth
knowth.summary: A prehistoric passage tomb near the River Boyne in Ireland, built around 3200 BC and holding Europe's largest collection of megalithic art, part of the Brú na Bóinne World Heritage Site.

dowth.name: Dowth
dowth.summary: A Neolithic passage tomb near the River Boyne in Ireland, one of three main tombs of the Brú na Bóinne site along with Newgrange and Knowth, dating to about 3200 BC.

county-meath.name: County Meath
county-meath.summary: A county in eastern Ireland known as 'The Royal County,' once the seat of Ireland's High Kings before being formally shired in 1297.

mike-parker-pearson.name: Mike Parker Pearson
mike-parker-pearson.summary: An English archaeologist specializing in Neolithic Britain and the archaeology of death and burial, known for directing the Stonehenge Riverside Project.

carrowmore.name: Carrowmore
carrowmore.summary: A large cluster of Neolithic megalithic tombs near Sligo, Ireland, built in the 4th millennium BC and among the largest groups of such tombs in the country.

post-track.name: Post Track
post-track.summary: An ancient timber causeway in England's Somerset Levels, dated to around 3838 BCE, roughly 30 years older than the nearby Sweet Track and likely meant as a permanent, maintained route.

r-ssen-culture.name: Rössen culture
r-ssen-culture.summary: A middle Neolithic culture of Central Europe, about 4600 to 4300 BCE, named after a burial site in Saxony-Anhalt and marking a shift toward more diverse later Neolithic cultures.

old-europe-archaeology.name: Old Europe
old-europe-archaeology.summary: A term coined by archaeologist Marija Gimbutas for a pre-Indo-European Neolithic and Copper Age culture centered in the Lower Danube Valley of Southeast Europe.
